subject: Re: IP indemnity carveout request - Dataset-Train v2
messages:
From: Emily Choi <emily.choi@firmcraft.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Rogers <ben.rogers@firmcraft.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 08:11:00 -0800
Subject: IP indemnity carveout request - Dataset-Train v2

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. We ran this up the chain and legal has a hard ask on the MSA: FirmCraft cannot accept the proposed scope of IP indemnity for model-training outputs derived from our proprietary datasets (Dataset-Train v2). Their position is that any downstream outputs that are substantially derived from our training set should be excluded from Redwood liability — they want a carveout or an alternative risk allocation (insurance/escrow/notice + remediation).

I've attached our redline (FirmCraft_MSA_Redline_v3.docx) with the relevant paragraph highlighted.

Can Redwood propose language that limits Redwood's indemnity for third-party claims tied to customer-supplied training data? If not, we need a commercial mitigation (purchase of insurance, escrow option, or an expanded indemnity cap tied to the customer dataset). This is a gating issue for procurement.

Are you able to escalate to legal and share an internal position + suggested compromise today or tomorrow? We have procurement review on Thursday.

Best,
Emily
Emily Choi
Head of Legal Ops, FirmCraft
emily.choi@firmcraft.com

Attachment: FirmCraft_MSA_Redline_v3.docx (MS Word, 48 KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Choi <emily.choi@firmcraft.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: IP indemnity carveout request - Dataset-Train v2

Emily — thanks for the clear note and for surfacing the redline. I appreciate the procurement timeline; we will prioritize.

Quick summary of Redwood's current posture: our standard MSA ties indemnity to third-party IP claims alleging infringement by the delivered services (including models Redwood hosts), with explicit carveouts for customer-supplied data that introduce third-party materials. That said, we typically do not accept a broad carveout that absolves us of all exposure tied to models trained or fine-tuned on customer data — customers often ask for that and procurement pushes back.

Proposed next steps:
- Kimberly: can you draft a compact alternative redline we can propose that narrows FirmCraft's ask to narrowly-scoped training-data-derived-outputs (definition + temporal boundary) and ties remediation to notice + cure rights instead of full-blown indemnity?
- Aditya: can you pull the revenue / discount thresholds and confirm whether this deal crosses our executive approval matrix if we put in an insurance or escrow obligation?
- Emily: can you confirm whether FirmCraft would consider (i) a capped indemnity specifically for claims attributable to Dataset-Train v2, or (ii) agreeing to maintain a specific insurance policy naming Redwood as an additional insured? Either would reduce commercial friction.

I am happy to join a short call with your procurement and legal if that moves things faster.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Choi <emily.choi@firmcraft.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: IP indemnity carveout request - Dataset-Train v2

Jonas / Aditya — looping in with proposed legal language and negotiation points. I kept it tight to minimize back-and-forth with procurement.

Key points for the redline:
1) Define "Customer Training Data" narrowly — only data specifically labeled in the order form as Dataset-Train v2 and ingested between dates X and Y.
2) Limit carveout scope to "Customer Training Data" that contains third-party proprietary content that the customer did not have the right to use.
3) Replace a blanket carveout with a two-track allocation: (a) Redwood will defend/reimburse for third-party claims to the extent such claims arise from Redwood's grossly negligent model modification or from failure of Redwood's delivery of a model version as specified in the order form; (b) for claims plausibly attributable to Customer Training Data, liability will be limited to direct damages capped at the lesser of $X or the fees paid for the affected service in the prior 12 months.
4) Require notice and cooperation: customer must deliver claim notice and all evidence; Redwood may elect to assume defense subject to cooperation and full control over settlement.
5) Commercial mitigation path: if customer requires broader indemnity, require (i) customer to procure and maintain insurance with minimum limits and Redwood named as an additional insured, or (ii) escrow of critical training artifacts with escrow release conditions tied to an adjudicated claim.

Proposed redline snippet to offer (to be inserted in IP/Indemnity section):
"For clarity, 'Customer Training Data' means only the datasets expressly identified in the Order Form as 'Dataset-Train v2' and used in the training of Customer-specific model artifacts during the period specified in the Order Form. Redwood's indemnity obligations shall not apply to claims arising solely from Customer Training Data unless (i) Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct contributed to such claim, or (ii) Customer fails to provide timely notice and cooperation. Where a claim is attributable in whole or in part to Customer Training Data, Redwood's aggregate liability for such claim shall be limited to direct damages not to exceed the lesser of $250,000 or the fees paid by Customer for the affected service in the prior 12 months."

Questions for Sales:
- Jonas: will FirmCraft accept a 12-month fees cap or do they need a fixed monetary cap (e.g., $1M)?
- Aditya: if we propose insurance, what's the minimum policy limit we should request for this tier? Our standard for equivalent exposure has been $2M occ./$5M aggregate in similar negotiations.

Attachments: Redwood_proposed_redline_IP_section.docx (proposed insertion + negotiation notes)

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
kimberly.park@redwood.com

On a separate note: preserve evidence chain — procurement will ask for a list of reproducible artifacts (hashes/ingest logs). If they require escrow, ops needs to know format and retention window.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Choi <emily.choi@firmcraft.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: IP indemnity carveout request - Dataset-Train v2

Quick commercial note — I pulled the numbers: FirmCraft is expected to commit $680k ARR in year one under the current order form. Offering an indemnity cap tied to 12 months of fees (~$680k) is feasible without executive exception. Asking for a $1M fixed cap would require Head of Sales + CFO signoff.

If Kimberly wants to push for insurance as the preferred mitigation, our recommendation for a single-customer deal of this magnitude is to request a $2M per-occurrence / $5M aggregate policy with Redwood named as additional insured. That will reduce the likelihood we need to accept a $1M+ fixed cap.

Also — escrow adds operational friction. If procurement insists on escrow of Dataset-Train v2 artifacts, we need to scope format (tarball containing ingest manifests + sample records) and retention (recommended: 24 months). Ops should weigh in on feasibility.

I'll flag this for escalation: because FirmCraft is asking to carve out training-data outputs, this is a material legal deviation with potential downstream risk — please let me know if either of you want me to schedule a triage call with Head of Legal (Marissa Cole) and Head of Sales (Rishi Malhotra) tomorrow morning.

Aditya Rao
Director, Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Attachment: pricing-impact-summary.xlsx (referenced in body)

Subject: Re: IP indemnity carveout request - Dataset-Train v2

Thanks Jonas / Kimberly / Aditya — that language is helpful and a good starting point. FirmCraft is open to a narrowly-defined carveout with the narrower definition you proposed, and a capped liability, but procurement needs explicit numeric commitments. They prefer a fixed cap over a fees-based formula for predictability.

FirmCraft can consider an insurance requirement instead of a $1M fixed cap, but we will need confirmation on policy language (who is named, scope of coverage). We are available for a 30-minute call tomorrow at 9:30 AM PT to walk legal + procurement through the proposed snippet and the insurance/escrow options.

Emily
